evidence.claim: Article 110 gives the Leader supreme command of the armed forces, war-and-peace authority, and appointment power over key judiciary, media, and military posts; Article 111 provides a temporary replacement council if the office becomes vacant.
evidence.title: Iran (Islamic Republic of) 1979 (rev. 1989) Constitution
evidence.excerpt: Article 110 gives the Leader supreme command of the armed forces, war-and-peace authority, and appointment power over key judiciary, media, and military posts; Article 111 provides a temporary replacement council if the office becomes vacant.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Stable constitutional text reproduced by a reputable legal repository; directly defines authority and constraints relevant to 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct office-level authority held by Ali Khamenei as Supreme Leader.
contrary_evidence: The constitution includes a formal vacancy-replacement mechanism, so the office is powerful but not literally unbounded on paper.

evidence.claim: Khamenei said Iran's economy should not be tied to efforts to remove U.S. sanctions and urged officials to govern so sanctions would not hurt the country, while promoting a knowledge-based economy and foreign trade.
evidence.title: Iran's Khamenei says economy should not be tied to U.S. sanctions
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei said Iran's economy should not be tied to efforts to remove U.S. sanctions and urged officials to govern so sanctions would not hurt the country, while promoting a knowledge-based economy and foreign trade.
evidence.source_locator: Reuters summary and quoted speech in the article text
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters wire quotes the supreme leader directly in a target-period speech.
evidence.period_fit: Exact target period, March 21, 2022 Nowruz speech.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Khamenei speech; strong ruler attribution.
contrary_evidence: A speech states intent and framing, not implementation or results.

evidence.claim: Khamenei used his New Year speech to call for knowledge-based production, job creation, higher productivity, and food self-sufficiency, saying production would improve growth, employment, inflation, and public welfare.
evidence.title: Leader: Iran's economy should not be tied to US sanctions, country must become impervious to bans
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei used his New Year speech to call for knowledge-based production, job creation, higher productivity, and food self-sufficiency, saying production would improve growth, employment, inflation, and public welfare.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official outlet quoting a televised speech with direct quotations; useful for intent but not independent on effects.
evidence.period_fit: Exact target period, March 2022 New Year message and follow-up speech.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Khamenei speech; strong attribution.
contrary_evidence: Official state-media framing may overstate policy coherence and success.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said Iran's economy was in gradual recovery, but consumer inflation was rising, the fiscal balance was still under pressure, growth remained modest, and lower-income households faced mounting welfare pressure; it recommended jobs, infrastructure, better business conditions, and targeted social transfers.
evidence.title: Iran Economic Monitor, Spring 2022: Managing Economic Uncertainties
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said Iran's economy was in gradual recovery, but consumer inflation was rising, the fiscal balance was still under pressure, growth remained modest, and lower-income households faced mounting welfare pressure; it recommended jobs, infrastructure, better business conditions, and targeted social transfers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary multilateral analysis with clear target-period macro and welfare assessment.
evidence.period_fit: Published in 2022 and describing 2021/22 conditions and 2022-24 outlook.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level policy context, not a direct Khamenei decision; useful for inherited constraints and outcome attribution limits.
contrary_evidence: The report notes some revenue improvement from higher oil and tax receipts, so the picture is not purely negative.

evidence.claim: The IMF paper found that currency depreciation, fiscal deficits, and sanctions were major drivers of inflation in Iran, and that large fiscal deficits, rapid liquidity growth, negative real interest rates, and distortive price controls worsened pressures; it recommended fiscal adjustment and stronger inflation targeting.
evidence.title: Determinants of Inflation in Iran and Policies to Curb It
evidence.excerpt: The IMF paper found that currency depreciation, fiscal deficits, and sanctions were major drivers of inflation in Iran, and that large fiscal deficits, rapid liquidity growth, negative real interest rates, and distortive price controls worsened pressures; it recommended fiscal adjustment and stronger inflation targeting.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IMF research summary with clear causal claims and policy implications, though the full article page was access-restricted.
evidence.period_fit: Uses 2004-2021 data and was published in 2022, so it fits as retrospective analysis of the target-year environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Macro-causal analysis, not direct ruler attribution; most useful as context for policy choices and constraints.
contrary_evidence: Research paper, not a finding of personal responsibility; it supports context more than command attribution.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that a cut in government wheat subsidies drove flour-staple price hikes as high as 300 percent, official inflation was around 40 percent, and almost half of Iran's population was below the poverty line, triggering protests and arrests.
evidence.title: Soaring bread prices spark protests and shop fires in Iran - IRNA
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that a cut in government wheat subsidies drove flour-staple price hikes as high as 300 percent, official inflation was around 40 percent, and almost half of Iran's population was below the poverty line, triggering protests and arrests.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting with concrete price, inflation, and poverty claims tied to a specific policy change.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to the May subsidy shock.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government policy and resulting hardship are attributable to the ruling system, but the article does not isolate Khamenei's personal role.
contrary_evidence: The article is based partly on official IRNA reporting and Reuters could not independently verify some social-media material.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that about 1,000 retirees protested peacefully over soaring living costs, that pensioners said a 57.4 percent increase was too little too late, and that the unrest reflected years of inflation and complaints about economic management and corruption.
evidence.title: Iranian pensioners protest against high living costs - reports
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that about 1,000 retirees protested peacefully over soaring living costs, that pensioners said a 57.4 percent increase was too little too late, and that the unrest reflected years of inflation and complaints about economic management and corruption.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting with specific crowd size, policy response, and hardship context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Primarily a government-performance signal; Khamenei attribution is structural rather than direct.
contrary_evidence: Crowd-size and social-media details were not independently verified by Reuters.

evidence.claim: The article said Iran's 2022 budget bill allocated more than 54.8 trillion tomans for public order and security, a 14 percent rise from the previous year and far more than environmental protection or water-crisis spending; the IRGC-linked Shahid Ebrahimi program also saw a roughly 386 percent increase.
evidence.title: Iran's Budget: 'Security and Order' Gets Six Times More Funding than 'Water Resources'
evidence.excerpt: The article said Iran's 2022 budget bill allocated more than 54.8 trillion tomans for public order and security, a 14 percent rise from the previous year and far more than environmental protection or water-crisis spending; the IRGC-linked Shahid Ebrahimi program also saw a roughly 386 percent increase.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent local data-analysis outlet with a specific budget comparison; the figures are concrete even if interpretation is editorialized.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Budget priorities are regime-level, not uniquely Khamenei's, but they are informative for elite preferences and distributional choices under his authority.
contrary_evidence: The article is partially paywalled and interpretive beyond the budget figures themselves.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that President Ebrahim Raisi approved the public budget for the Iranian year beginning March 20, with the plan targeting 8 percent growth and 1.2 million bpd of crude sales despite continued U.S. sanctions, while assuming sanctions would persist.
evidence.title: Iran's president approves public budget
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that President Ebrahim Raisi approved the public budget for the Iranian year beginning March 20, with the plan targeting 8 percent growth and 1.2 million bpd of crude sales despite continued U.S. sanctions, while assuming sanctions would persist.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters wire gives a concrete budget target and explicit sanctions assumption.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is Raisi's budget, not Khamenei's direct decision, so attribution to the supreme leader is indirect.
contrary_evidence: The article does not show whether the target was realistic or implemented.

evidence.claim: Iran appointed Mohammad Reza Farzin as central bank governor; he came from Bank Melli, and the appointment was made in the cabinet amid a record-low rial and inflation around 50 percent.
evidence.title: Iran appoints new central bank chief
evidence.excerpt: Iran appointed Mohammad Reza Farzin as central bank governor; he came from Bank Melli, and the appointment was made in the cabinet amid a record-low rial and inflation around 50 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with specific appointment and macroeconomic trigger, but still a syndication host rather than the original Reuters page.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level appointment under the broader system; Khamenei's role is indirect through regime authority rather than shown in the article.
contrary_evidence: The article does not prove the governor change improved inflation or exchange-rate performance.

evidence.claim: In his first public comments on the protests, Khamenei called them riots, blamed the United States and Israel, and said the death of Mahsa Amini had broken his heart while still denying that the unrest reflected normal public reaction.
evidence.title: Iran's Khamenei blames Israel, US in first comments on protests
evidence.excerpt: In his first public comments on the protests, Khamenei called them riots, blamed the United States and Israel, and said the death of Mahsa Amini had broken his heart while still denying that the unrest reflected normal public reaction.
evidence.source_locator: middle paragraphs containing the quoted speech
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-reported speech with direct quotation and strong contemporaneous corroboration.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Khamenei public statement.
contrary_evidence: He did acknowledge Amini’s death as painful, which is a limited sign of acknowledgment.
The speech still sharply shifted responsibility away from the state and toward foreign enemies.

evidence.claim: Khamenei praised Basij forces for sacrificing themselves to save people from rioters, explicitly endorsing the militia wing that was central to protest suppression.
evidence.title: Iran's Khamenei praises Basij forces for confronting 'riots'
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei praised Basij forces for sacrificing themselves to save people from rioters, explicitly endorsing the militia wing that was central to protest suppression.
evidence.source_locator: first paragraphs of the Reuters wire
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with direct quotation and clear context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Khamenei public statement.
contrary_evidence: This is supportive of repression, not evidence of personal honesty.
It helps mainly as evidence of tolerance and endorsement of the crackdown narrative.

evidence.claim: OFAC said seven senior leaders in Iran’s government and security apparatus were responsible for shutting down Iran’s internet access and continuing violence against peaceful protesters; the release specifically named the interior minister, communications minister, and an IRGC-linked close associate of the Supreme Leader’s orbit.
evidence.title: Treasury Sanctions Iranian Leaders Responsible for Internet Shutdown and Violent Crackdown on Peaceful Protests
evidence.excerpt: OFAC said seven senior leaders in Iran’s government and security apparatus were responsible for shutting down Iran’s internet access and continuing violence against peaceful protesters; the release specifically named the interior minister, communications minister, and an IRGC-linked close associate of the Supreme Leader’s orbit.
evidence.source_locator: main release text and sanctions rationale sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary U.S. government sanctions notice with specific named roles and rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the named officials acted inside the Khamenei-led system; not a direct personal order from Khamenei in the document.
contrary_evidence: The document does not name Khamenei himself as the actor.
It is a sanctions finding, so it is adversarial but still primary evidence.

evidence.claim: Treasury said the Iranian government cut off internet access for most citizens to prevent the world from watching its crackdown on peaceful protesters, and the license was issued to help Iranians access outside platforms and services.
evidence.title: U.S. Treasury Issues Iran General License D-2 to Increase Support for Internet Freedom
evidence.excerpt: Treasury said the Iranian government cut off internet access for most citizens to prevent the world from watching its crackdown on peaceful protesters, and the license was issued to help Iranians access outside platforms and services.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and Deputy Secretary quotation
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary U.S. government statement with explicit causal language about concealment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the action is attributed to the Iranian government under Khamenei’s system.
contrary_evidence: The document is a U.S. policy statement, not an internal Iranian record.
It does not isolate Khamenei personally from the broader regime action.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Khamenei controlled Setad, a vast business empire worth about $95 billion, and that the organization expanded under him with final resources independent of parliament and the national budget.
evidence.title: Exclusive: Reuters investigates business empire of Iran's supreme leader
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Khamenei controlled Setad, a vast business empire worth about $95 billion, and that the organization expanded under him with final resources independent of parliament and the national budget.
evidence.source_locator: middle and later paragraphs on Setad’s scope, control, and lack of supervision
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major Reuters investigation with detailed documentary and interview basis, though not in the target year.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 structural background that still frames the 2022 period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for long-running Khamenei control over the structure; not proof of personal cash enrichment.
contrary_evidence: Reuters said there was no evidence Khamenei personally tapped Setad to enrich himself.
Because it predates 2022, it is background rather than target-period conduct.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Setad was close to Iran’s ruling elite, that Khamenei exerted exclusive control over its economic empire and chose its executives, and that the structure was used to fund hardline leverage and bypass normal government branches.
evidence.title: Conglomerate controlled by Iran's supreme leader a winner from nuclear deal
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Setad was close to Iran’s ruling elite, that Khamenei exerted exclusive control over its economic empire and chose its executives, and that the structure was used to fund hardline leverage and bypass normal government branches.
evidence.source_locator: paragraphs describing Setad’s control and governance
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with explicit attribution and structural detail.
evidence.period_fit: Structural background relevant to 2022, though published earlier.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for Khamenei’s control over the Setad network; still not a personal asset disclosure.
contrary_evidence: The article also says Reuters found no evidence of personal enrichment.
Its date means it should be used as inherited-structure context, not fresh 2022 conduct.

evidence.claim: Khamenei set the 2022 year slogan around production that is knowledge-based and job-creating, said past emphasis on production had produced good results, and urged officials to turn the slogan into real policy rather than decoration.
evidence.title: Production should be knowledge-based and job-creating in the year 1401 SH
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei set the 2022 year slogan around production that is knowledge-based and job-creating, said past emphasis on production had produced good results, and urged officials to turn the slogan into real policy rather than decoration.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct reproduction of the Supreme Leader's Nowruz message with dated, attributable text and clear policy language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Khamenei statement; strong attribution for program identification and priorities.
contrary_evidence: This is a program statement, not proof of execution.
It still relies on official self-report for the claimed prior-year success.

evidence.claim: Iran's 2022 budget bill allocated more than 54.8 trillion tomans for public order and security, a 14 percent increase, and the Shahid Ebrahimi security-infrastructure program rose about 386 percent year over year.
evidence.title: Iran's Budget: Security and Order Gets Six Times More Funding than Water Resources
evidence.excerpt: Iran's 2022 budget bill allocated more than 54.8 trillion tomans for public order and security, a 14 percent increase, and the Shahid Ebrahimi security-infrastructure program rose about 386 percent year over year.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Quantified budget analysis with a clear 2022 fiscal claim, though it is an interpretive policy analysis rather than an official budget PDF.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Structural but relevant: this reflects ruling-network priorities under Khamenei's authority, not a personal instruction from him.
contrary_evidence: It shows security prioritization, not whether the spending was efficient or effective.
The article is advocacy-adjacent analysis, so it needs corroboration.

evidence.claim: Iranian oil exports rose above 1 million barrels per day for the first time in almost three years, showing the regime could sustain significant sanctioned oil flows to China despite U.S. pressure.
evidence.title: As nuclear talks resume, Iran's oil exports increase
evidence.excerpt: Iranian oil exports rose above 1 million barrels per day for the first time in almost three years, showing the regime could sustain significant sanctioned oil flows to China despite U.S. pressure.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with precise quantified export estimates from tanker-tracking firms.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to 2022 output and early-year trajectory.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the result reflects regime policy and sanctions-evasion capacity under Khamenei's system, not a personal order in the article.
contrary_evidence: Reuters notes the exports still depended on sanction evasion and did not prove a durable policy solution.
The figure is an estimate, not an official Iranian statistic.

evidence.claim: Iran's crude exports in December 2022 averaged 1.137 million barrels per day, the highest 2022 figure reported by SVB International, and exports had hit the highest since 2019 on some estimates.
evidence.title: Iranian oil exports end 2022 at a high, despite no nuclear deal
evidence.excerpt: Iran's crude exports in December 2022 averaged 1.137 million barrels per day, the highest 2022 figure reported by SVB International, and exports had hit the highest since 2019 on some estimates.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with a concrete year-end estimate from an industry tracker and explicit comparison to prior years.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective but directly about the end of 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: it reflects the outcome of sanctions-resistance policy under Khamenei's regime rather than an individual command document.
contrary_evidence: The source attributes part of the rise to market conditions and sanctions enforcement gaps, not just Iranian competence.
It remains an estimate rather than a state-released figure.

evidence.claim: Iran appointed Mohammad Reza Farzin as central bank chief; the report noted his Bank Melli background and said the appointment came amid a record-low rial and inflation around 50 percent.
evidence.title: Iran appoints new central bank chief
evidence.excerpt: Iran appointed Mohammad Reza Farzin as central bank chief; the report noted his Bank Melli background and said the appointment came amid a record-low rial and inflation around 50 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with a concrete appointment and contemporaneous macroeconomic context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Structural but relevant: the appointment reflects regime response and personnel choice under Khamenei's system, not a direct Khamenei quote.
contrary_evidence: This shows adaptation, but in response to failure rather than clear success.
The report does not prove the new appointee improved outcomes by year-end.

evidence.claim: Iran's judiciary said courts would deal firmly with protesters, and the report said more than 1,000 people had been indicted in Tehran Province alone in connection with the unrest.
evidence.title: Iran's judiciary says it will deal firmly with protesters
evidence.excerpt: Iran's judiciary said courts would deal firmly with protesters, and the report said more than 1,000 people had been indicted in Tehran Province alone in connection with the unrest.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with specific numbers and contemporaneous protest-response details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the judiciary is part of the Khamenei-led regime's enforcement apparatus.
contrary_evidence: This shows coercive control more than administrative competence in a policy sense.
It does not show whether the response resolved the underlying unrest.

evidence.claim: The EU said Iranian authorities severely restricted internet access and blocked instant messaging platforms during the protests, which it said violated freedom of expression and should be stopped immediately.
evidence.title: Iran: Declaration by the High Representative on Behalf of the E.U.
evidence.excerpt: The EU said Iranian authorities severely restricted internet access and blocked instant messaging platforms during the protests, which it said violated freedom of expression and should be stopped immediately.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official EU declaration with direct, dated attribution of the internet restrictions and an explicit description of the harm.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Structural but material: the action was by Iranian authorities under Khamenei's system, not a direct personal order in the document.
contrary_evidence: The source condemns the action rather than evaluating whether it helped the regime maintain control.
It does not establish a direct link to a named individual beyond the authorities.

evidence.claim: OFAC designated Iran's Morality Police and seven senior security officials, saying these bodies routinely used violence to suppress protesters and other civil-society groups and were responsible for Amini's death and the crackdown.
evidence.title: Treasury Sanctions Iran’s Morality Police and Senior Security Officials for Violence Against Protesters and the Death of Mahsa Amini
evidence.excerpt: OFAC designated Iran's Morality Police and seven senior security officials, saying these bodies routinely used violence to suppress protesters and other civil-society groups and were responsible for Amini's death and the crackdown.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary U.S. sanctions notice with concrete names, organizational roles, and detailed rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the named security organs are part of the regime Khamenei oversees; the document does not prove a direct personal command from him.
contrary_evidence: This is an adversarial sanctions finding, so the language is not neutral.
It proves coercive implementation more clearly than strategic planning competence.

evidence.claim: Iran acknowledged it had supplied Moscow with drones before the war in Ukraine, and the report said Russia had used them to attack power stations and civilian infrastructure.
evidence.title: Iran acknowledges drone shipments to Russia before war, Kyiv says Tehran is lying
evidence.excerpt: Iran acknowledged it had supplied Moscow with drones before the war in Ukraine, and the report said Russia had used them to attack power stations and civilian infrastructure.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with explicit acknowledgment and direct linkage to battlefield use.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022, with a near-term retrospective statement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: this reflects a regime-level foreign-policy and military-support decision under Khamenei's umbrella.
contrary_evidence: Iran said the drones were sent before the war, so the precise timing is contested.
The article does not identify Khamenei personally as the decision-maker.

evidence.claim: The United States said companies and people were involved in the production or transfer of Iranian drones used by Russia, and it identified the Shahed Aviation Industries Research Center as subordinate to the IRGC Aerospace Force.
evidence.title: U.S. targets supply of Iranian drones to Russia in new sanctions
evidence.excerpt: The United States said companies and people were involved in the production or transfer of Iranian drones used by Russia, and it identified the Shahed Aviation Industries Research Center as subordinate to the IRGC Aerospace Force.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with named entities, clear sanctions rationale, and specific organizational attribution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the entities are part of the Khamenei-led security network, though not a direct personal order in the report.
contrary_evidence: The article reports U.S. sanctions allegations rather than an internal Iranian admission.
It measures foreign-policy execution, not domestic governance competence.

evidence.claim: The U.S. Commerce Department said three Iranian cargo planes serving Russia were transporting goods, including electronics, to Russia in apparent violation of export controls, and that Iran had publicly announced plans to expand aviation cooperation with Russia.
evidence.title: U.S. adds Iran cargo planes flying to Russia to export violation list
evidence.excerpt: The U.S. Commerce Department said three Iranian cargo planes serving Russia were transporting goods, including electronics, to Russia in apparent violation of export controls, and that Iran had publicly announced plans to expand aviation cooperation with Russia.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire based on a U.S. Commerce Department statement and commercially available tracking data.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: it reflects a regime-linked aviation/logistics network under Khamenei's broader authority.
contrary_evidence: The underlying data are indirect and not a direct Iranian confession.
The activity is relevant to influence and sanctions evasion, not to broad domestic effectiveness.

evidence.claim: Britain sanctioned three Iranian military figures and a defense manufacturer for supplying Russia with drones to attack civilian and infrastructure targets in Ukraine, saying the individuals were personally responsible for the provision.
evidence.title: Britain sanctions Iran over supply of drones to Russia
evidence.excerpt: Britain sanctioned three Iranian military figures and a defense manufacturer for supplying Russia with drones to attack civilian and infrastructure targets in Ukraine, saying the individuals were personally responsible for the provision.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with specific sanctioning of named individuals and a clear statement of personal responsibility.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material: the sanctioned officers belong to the Khamenei-aligned security apparatus, though the article does not prove a direct personal order.
contrary_evidence: This is adversarial sanctions evidence rather than neutral monitoring.
It demonstrates military-influence execution more than civilian policy competence.

evidence.claim: Khamenei issued policies aimed at improving social welfare, reducing poverty, and supporting vulnerable groups, and ordered the executive branch to produce an implementation plan within six months.
evidence.title: Iran's Khamenei Issues Decree To Set Up A Social Safety Net
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei issued policies aimed at improving social welfare, reducing poverty, and supporting vulnerable groups, and ordered the executive branch to produce an implementation plan within six months.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous report on a specific decree, but from a media outlet rather than the original Persian text.
evidence.period_fit: directly in 2022 and within the target ruler-period
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable: the proclamation is presented as Khamenei's own directive to the heads of power; it shows personal agenda-setting, not proof of delivery.
contrary_evidence: The article notes no dedicated funding and says the directive is a brief, general guideline.

evidence.claim: Khamenei outlined the 7th development plan as a five-year program centered on economic progress with justice and an 8 percent growth target, with food-security and national information-network measures among the stated priorities.
evidence.title: Leader Communicates General Policies of Iran's 7th Development Plan
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei outlined the 7th development plan as a five-year program centered on economic progress with justice and an 8 percent growth target, with food-security and national information-network measures among the stated priorities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The report quotes and summarizes a specific proclamation and gives detailed policy content, though it is still a news report rather than the original decree text.
evidence.period_fit: directly in 2022 and within the target ruler-period
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable: the item reports a proclamation by Khamenei sent to top state leaders, reflecting his agenda-setting power.
contrary_evidence: The article describes planned goals; it does not prove implementation or attainment in 2022.
Later macro outcomes remained stressed by inflation and hardship in other sources.

evidence.claim: Iran's child social protection system was presented as targeting vulnerable households, especially in less advantaged provinces, using a welfare database of deprived households and a cash-plus model in selected provinces.
evidence.title: UNICEF and Ministry of Labour discussed enhancing social protection systems for children
evidence.excerpt: Iran's child social protection system was presented as targeting vulnerable households, especially in less advantaged provinces, using a welfare database of deprived households and a cash-plus model in selected provinces.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF is an official UN agency and the page describes a specific national policy discussion and implementation architecture.
evidence.period_fit: directly in 2022 and within the target ruler-period
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant: this shows the state apparatus and welfare ministry implementing a child social-protection architecture under the Supreme Leader's governing framework, but it is not a personal decree from Khamenei.
contrary_evidence: This describes a webinar and system presentation, not an independent outcome evaluation.
It does not quantify coverage gains or prove Khamenei's direct day-to-day management.

evidence.claim: UNHCR says all children in Iran have access to primary and secondary education regardless of documentation status, and that it co-funded 81 schools in refugee-populated areas between 2016 and 2022.
evidence.title: Education
evidence.excerpt: UNHCR says all children in Iran have access to primary and secondary education regardless of documentation status, and that it co-funded 81 schools in refugee-populated areas between 2016 and 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNHCR is the relevant UN agency and the page contains specific operational claims about access and school construction, though it is a current web page rather than a dated 2022 report.
evidence.period_fit: policy and implementation context spans 2016-2022 and remains relevant to the 2022 period
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect: this is evidence of government-compatible refugee access policy and UNHCR implementation in Iran, but not direct proof that Khamenei personally ran the program day to day.
contrary_evidence: The page is not time-stamped for 2022 and does not provide household survey outcomes.
It does not isolate Khamenei from broader state or UNHCR implementation.

evidence.claim: In July 2022, Iran ran a targeted measles vaccination campaign for children and vulnerable communities; refugee families without immigration documents were vaccinated, and the article says confirmed cases fell dramatically.
evidence.title: Health workers in Iran reach out to families of children with measles to vaccinate all family member
evidence.excerpt: In July 2022, Iran ran a targeted measles vaccination campaign for children and vulnerable communities; refugee families without immigration documents were vaccinated, and the article says confirmed cases fell dramatically.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF provides a dated field story with concrete operational details, named beneficiaries, and an explicit 2022 campaign result, though it is still a program story rather than an audit.
evidence.period_fit: directly in 2022 and within the target ruler-period
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but meaningful: the campaign shows government health services functioning for refugees and vulnerable households under the regime, but it does not isolate Khamenei's personal operational role.
contrary_evidence: The evidence is narrative and does not independently audit causality for the decline in cases.
It does not show whether the campaign was ordered by Khamenei rather than the health ministry.
